mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without any threshold condition.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS decline in the prior month correlates with negative 20-day SPX returns in more than 50% of instances over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate and declining unemployment rate indicates an overheating economy, which triggers a negative S&P 500 return over the next 20 days due to imminent monetary tightening.
failure_condition: The joint movement of FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE falling fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in housing starts below 1.2 million units signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST decline below 1.2 million in late-cycle expansion does not correlate with negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly job growth, measured by PAYEMS exceeding 150,000 new jobs, consistently drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days by boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth above 150,000 fails to produce positive 5-day SPX returns in more than 50% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production below -0.5% signals a weakening supply chain, which reduces inflation expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO decline below -0.5% fails to predict positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime, a decline in retail sales (RSAFS) below 0.2% monthly growth indicates weakening consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS decline below 0.2% in high-inflation regimes does not correlate with negative 20-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher inflation levels, as measured by CPIAUCSL, indicate a strong economy and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to real rate adjustments and corporate pricing power.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL level fails to correlate positively with 5-day SPX returns in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.
